evidence: Phaedr. 3.7.5: aut quō cibō fēcistī tantum corporis?
terms.comment: With a noun: quod pōculum?, which cup? Without a noun the pronoun is quis, quid, and “which of them?” is quis eōrum? or quis ex eīs?.

terms.grammar: interrogative pronoun and adjective; genitive utrīus, dative utrī
evidence: Plaut. Men. 1119: Uter erātis, tūn' an ille, major?
Plaut. Aul. 321: sed uter vestrōrum est celerior?
terms.comment: Latin has a word for the choice between two; quis is for more than two (Lewis & Short).

phrases.latin: unde sīc, quaesō, nitēs? aut quō cibō fēcistī tantum corporis?
phrases.english: where do you get that shine, tell me? What food has made you so big?

phrases.latin: quem ex eīs vultis in cēnam statim fierī?
phrases.english: which of them do you want made into dinner straight away?

phrases.latin: Uter erātis, tūn' an ille, major?
phrases.english: Which of you was the elder, you or he?

phrases.latin: sed uter vestrōrum est celerior? memorā mihi.
phrases.english: but which of you two is quicker? Tell me.
